correctness.rationale: If a center belongs to a fort, every leaf adjacent to it must also belong or would have exactly one neighbour in the fort; such a fort then strictly contains a two-leaf fort and is not minimal. With both centers absent, the fort condition is exactly that neither leaf-class intersection has size one. Every nonempty fort therefore contains a same-side leaf pair, proving that the minimal forts are precisely those pairs. The resulting fort hypergraph is \(K_a\sqcup K_b\): its matching, fractional transversal and transversal numbers give the three claimed invariants, and the optimum face of a clique's fractional vertex-cover LP gives the optimizer classification. Fresh independent enumeration for all 2<=a,b<=4 recovered exactly these minimal forts.

value.rationale: Double stars are the simplest diameter-three trees with two branching centers. The exact fort hypergraph gives more than the general leaf bound: it determines every fractional optimum and shows the fort-cover integrality gap approaching two already in this elementary tree family, a natural extremal benchmark for the new relaxation.
residual_risks: A bistar/double-star computation may exist in unindexed zero-forcing literature under a family alias.

final_claim: For every double star D_a,b with a,b at least two, the minimal forts are exactly same-side leaf pairs, so the fort hypergraph is the disjoint union of K_a and K_b; consequently the fort number, fractional zero-forcing number, ordinary zero-forcing number, all fractional optimizers and the asymptotic integrality gap are exactly as stated.
limitations: Proper double stars with at least two leaves on each side only.
The parameter is the fort-cover LP fractional zero-forcing number, not the older three-colour forcing parameter.
